name: Marketplace integrity — seller velocity, refund/return-window features
category: Adjacent — abuse on the SUPPLY side of marketplaces
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Marketplace supply-side integrity (per-seller listing velocity, per-seller refund / cancellation / chargeback rate over rolling windows, per-(seller, buyer) collusion-pair counters, per-listing image-reuse and duplicate-detection counters, return-abuse counters, drop-shipping velocity signatures, ban-evasion / multi-account signals)
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A marketplace Trust & Safety / Marketplace Integrity service decides on every seller signup, listing create, edit, price-change, payout, refund, return claim, chargeback and policy-violation report — typically within 50-500 ms on the inline write path and seconds on the moderation-queue path — whether to approve, throttle, queue for review, suspend or claw back payout, based on per-seller / per-listing / per-(seller, buyer) / per-(seller, IP, device) rolling velocity, refund-rate, return-rate, distinct-counter and distribution features.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Detect and throttle high-velocity seller onboarding and listing creation - 'this newly-registered seller posted 500 listings in 1 hour from 3 IPs and 4 device fingerprints' - the canonical drop-shipping / counterfeit-burst / impersonation-burst signal called out by Walmart, eBay, Amazon, and Mercari T&S teams. 2) Compute per-seller rolling refund-rate, return-rate, INR (Item Not Received) rate, A-to-Z claim rate, chargeback rate, cancellation rate and Negative-Feedback Rate over 7d/30d/90d windows, threshold them against category-specific limits (Amazon's category-specific 5-8 % rolling-return-rate threshold, Walmart's published Seller Performance Standards on Cancellation Rate / On-Time Delivery / Valid Tracking / Seller Response / Return Rate / INR Rate / Negative Feedback Rate), and trigger suspension or returnless-refund forced settings. 3) Detect per-(seller, buyer) collusion pairs and friend-fraud (same buyer N times against same seller, or N seller accounts all paying out to the same beneficiary) via composite-key counters. 4) Detect listing-image reuse / duplicate-listing fraud by maintaining per-image-pHash counters across sellers and per-(seller, image_hash) counters: 'this seller's image_hash has been seen on 12 other suspended-seller accounts in the last 30 days.' 5) Detect ban-evasion / multi-accounting by counting per-(IP-prefix, device_fp, location_h3, payout_account) n_unique(seller_id) over rolling windows - the core signal that Incognia, Sift, and in-house teams build their seller-fraud stack on. 6) Feed downstream ML chargeback-guarantee and risk-score models (Riskified, Forter, Signifyd, Sift, in-house XGBoost) with a consistent rolling-feature view across the inline checkout / payout path and the analyst case-review path. 7) Power adaptive seller-friction: hold payout escrow, require additional KYB / document verification, force returnless-refund mode, or auto-suspend, based on continuously updated real-time features rather than the daily-batch performance dashboards most marketplaces ship today.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical events landing in beava as @bv.event: seller_signup {ts, seller_id, business_name, country, ip_hash, fp, device_id, payout_account_hash, email_domain, phone_hash, kyb_doc_hash, beneficial_owner_hash[]}, listing_create {ts, seller_id, listing_id, category, title_hash, description_hash, image_hashes[] (pHash/PDQ), price, brand, sku, gtin, location_h3, currency}, listing_edit {ts, seller_id, listing_id, fields_changed[], price_delta, title_change_bool}, listing_publish / takedown / soft-delete, price_change {ts, seller_id, listing_id, old_price, new_price}, order {ts, seller_id, buyer_id, listing_id, gmv, payment_method, ship_to_h3, ip_hash}, ship_event {ts, seller_id, order_id, carrier, tracking_id, valid_tracking_bool}, delivery_confirmed / INR_filed, return_initiated {ts, seller_id, buyer_id, order_id, reason_code, value, return_window_days_remaining}, return_completed, refund {ts, seller_id, order_id, value, refund_type (full|partial|returnless), initiated_by (seller|buyer|platform)}, chargeback / A_to_Z_claim / dispute, payout {ts, seller_id, value, beneficiary_account_hash, country_iso}, message {ts, sender_id, recipient_id, channel (on_platform|off_platform_attempt), contains_external_contact_bool}, review_create {ts, reviewer_id, seller_id, rating, text_hash, has_media_bool}, policy_violation_report {ts, reporter_id, seller_id|listing_id, reason_code}. Volume is dominated by listing_create, listing_edit, order, message, review_create. Distinct key dimensions: seller_id, listing_id, image_hash, (seller_id, buyer_id) pair, (seller_id, payout_account_hash) pair, (ip_hash, device_fp), beneficial_owner_hash, brand+gtin, category. This shape maps directly onto how Walmart, Amazon, eBay, Mercari, Etsy, Vinted, Whatnot, and Reverb describe their public seller-monitoring surface.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Heavy use of beava counters + velocity + n_unique + distribution primitives over sliding windows tied to platform performance-standard windows (1m / 1h / 24h / 7d / 30d / 90d). Per-seller: count(listing_create, 1h/24h/7d), velocity(listing_create) (drop-shipping signature), count(listing_edit, 1h) (price-pump / bait-and-switch), n_unique(category, 24h) (category-hopping is a low-quality / counterfeit signal), count(order, 7d/30d), sum(gmv, 30d), count(refund, 30d/90d) and refund_rate = count(refund, 30d) / count(order, 30d) - the canonical performance metric Amazon, Walmart and eBay enforce against - count(return_initiated, 30d/90d), return_rate, count(INR_filed, 30d), INR_rate, count(chargeback, 90d), chargeback_rate, count(A_to_Z_claim, 60d), n_unique(buyer_id, 7d) (low-fan-out is a money-laundering / wash-trade signal), n_unique(ship_to_h3, 30d), distribution(reason_code, 90d) (refund-reason entropy), count(off_platform_message_attempt, 7d), count(price_change, 24h), velocity(payout, 7d). Per-listing / per-image: count(view, 1h/24h), count(image_hash_seen_on_other_seller, lifetime) - the core duplicate-listing signal - n_unique(seller_id_using_this_image_hash, 90d), count(listing_takedown, lifetime per listing), distance(price_vs_category_median, current). Per-(seller, buyer) pair: count(order, 90d), sum(gmv, 90d), count(refund, 90d), count(positive_review, 90d) - high values on a pair flag wash-trading, friend-fraud and review-collusion. Per-(seller, payout_account_hash) and per-(payout_account_hash, n_unique(seller_id)): the canonical 'one bad actor running 30 seller accounts' signature flagged by Sift, Incognia, and Amazon Counterfeit Crimes Unit. Per-(ip_hash | device_fp | location_h3 | beneficial_owner_hash): n_unique(seller_id, 30d), count(seller_signup, 24h) - ban-evasion / device-farm signature. Per-brand+gtin: n_unique(seller_id, 30d) (unauthorized-reseller / counterfeit-burst signal feeding eBay 3PM Shield, Amazon Brand Registry, Doppel-style brand-protection workflows). Distance primitive on impossible-travel between seller_signup and listing_create locations.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite and high-cardinality. Primary keys are seller_id, listing_id, image_hash (pHash / PDQ / NeuralHash), brand+gtin, beneficial_owner_hash, payout_account_hash, and ordered pairs (seller_id, buyer_id), (seller_id, payout_account_hash), (seller_id, image_hash), (image_hash, seller_id_count) inverted-index style, (ip_hash, seller_id), (device_fp, seller_id), (location_h3, seller_id), (brand_gtin, seller_id). The (seller, buyer) pair, image_hash inverted view, and (payout_account, seller_id) inverted view are the marketplace-specific grains that distinguish item 10 from generic e-commerce fraud (item 1a) - they require composite-key first-class support.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Sliding windows dominate and must align with platform performance-standard windows: 1m / 1h (onboarding-burst), 24h (listing-burst), 7d (Walmart-style Cancellation Rate / On-Time Delivery), 30d (Amazon's rolling-return-rate threshold of 5-8 % per category, eBay seller performance defect rate), 60d / 90d (Amazon A-to-Z claim rate, chargeback windows), 180d / 365d (long-term seller trust scores, recidivism). Approximate aggregates (HLL for n_unique(buyer_id) per seller, n_unique(seller_id) per image_hash, n_unique(seller_id) per payout_account; CMS for top-K offending image_hashes / payout_accounts; T-Digest for refund-rate distributions across the seller population) are acceptable on the high-cardinality axes - thresholding decisions are monotonic in the count and 1-3 % HLL error is invisible against the moderator's threshold. Session / activity-burst windows are useful for the 'this newly-registered seller posted 500 listings in the first 6 hours then went silent' pattern. Tumbling windows show up for DSA transparency-report aggregation and for the daily / weekly Amazon-Walmart-eBay seller-scorecard dashboards.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Mixed. At-least-once with idempotent counters keyed on event_id is sufficient for velocity and rate features (a duplicate-counted refund biases the seller's refund-rate slightly upward, which is safe). Strict no-double-count is required only for (a) the actual payout-clawback and chargeback-loss-attribution numbers - which most marketplaces source from the financial ledger, not from beava - and (b) DSA / KYBC regulator transparency reports, which are batch-materialized off Parquet event logs.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Three operating points. (a) Inline write path (seller_signup, listing_create, listing_edit, message send): p99 < 100 ms feature-fetch is comfortable, p99 < 50 ms is required if velocity checks gate the action (Sift, Forter, Riskified, Signifyd all advertise sub-second inline decisions; for the listing-create surface 30-50 ms is the typical UX budget). (b) Inline checkout / payout path: p99 < 200 ms (chargeback-guarantee vendors operate under tight payment-flow SLAs). (c) Asynchronous moderator queue / payout-hold / suspension review: seconds-to-tens-of-seconds is fine. Beava's published sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits all three budgets with headroom.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Single-digit seconds end-to-end for the inline write and payout paths; sub-minute for the moderator-queue path. Coordinated counterfeit / drop-shipping bursts publicly described by Walmart and Amazon ramp in minutes (hundreds-to-thousands of fake listings in under an hour, per the CNBC 2025 Walmart Marketplace investigation), so stale features defeat detection. Beava's push-on-event model with no broker hop is materially fresher than the Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pipeline Riskified, Sift, and most in-house marketplaces publish about. [uncertain]
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Highly buyer-dependent. A mid-sized marketplace (Vinted, Depop, Mercari US, Reverb, Whatnot) reports listing-create and message volumes in the low thousands EPS at peak; Etsy, eBay, Walmart Marketplace, Amazon 3P, AliExpress aggregate to tens of thousands of EPS on the seller-action / listing-create surface alone, plus orders, returns, reviews, and messages. For a single mid-sized buyer, sustained ingest is typically 500-20k EPS with bursts to 100k EPS during coordinated counterfeit raids or seasonal surges; a single beava node at the published ~684k EPS (M4, TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) comfortably covers that. Sift publicly cites processing ~1T events per year across its entire customer base (~30k EPS amortized, with much higher per-customer peaks). Global platforms (Amazon 3P, AliExpress, eBay, Walmart Marketplace) are on a different scale entirely and would need horizontal partitioning that beava v0 does not yet ship. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly 1:1 to 5:1 reads-per-write on the inline write path (each seller_signup / listing_create / order / refund triggers one write and one batch_get of 20-80 features to score the action against rules + ML). Read-heavier (20:1+) on the analyst case-review and seller-scorecard dashboards where the same per-seller features are re-fetched repeatedly. Overall balanced-to-read-leaning, similar to the trust-and-safety item 9 shape.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Dominated by seller_id, listing_id, and image_hash cardinality, plus the explosive (seller, buyer) pair space. A mid-sized marketplace (~5M live sellers, ~50M live listings, ~50M live buyers): ~5M sellers × ~80-150 active counter slots × ~32 B per slot ~= 12-25 GB hot seller state; ~50M listings × ~10 counters ~= 15-20 GB listing state; ~50M unique active image_hashes × ~5 counters ~= 8 GB image-hash state; (seller, buyer) pair state capped via TTL because most pairs are one-shot. Total 50-150 GB live hot state on a single box for a mid-sized buyer - fits in RAM on a 256-512 GB machine but requires aggressive TTL eviction of cold sellers / closed listings / one-shot pairs. Global platforms (Amazon 3P with ~9M sellers worldwide, eBay with ~18M sellers, AliExpress, Walmart) blow well past a single beava node. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Slowly-growing on seller_id (signup-rate-bounded), explosive on listing_id (Amazon-3P scale is hundreds of millions of active listings; TTL on listing-level counters is mandatory after the listing closes), explosive on (seller, buyer) pair (long-tail), bounded-mid on brand+gtin and category, bounded on payout_account_hash (most sellers have 1-3) but with critical inverted-index n_unique(seller_id) per payout_account that is the load-bearing fraud signal. Image_hash cardinality is bounded by the catalog (and ideally compressed via near-duplicate clustering) but with a heavy tail. Top-K offending IPs / fingerprints / payout_accounts are CMS-appropriate.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Mixed TTLs aligned with platform performance windows. Hot velocity on seller / listing: 1m-7d sliding. Seller-performance metrics (refund-rate, return-rate, INR-rate, chargeback-rate): 30d / 60d / 90d rolling because Amazon, Walmart, and eBay all enforce on those windows. Per-(seller, buyer) collusion features: 90-180 days. Per-image-hash duplicate counters: lifetime-of-listing plus a long-tail post-takedown window (60-90 days) for ban-evasion detection. Per-payout-account inverted view: 12-24 months because beneficial-owner fraud rings can lie dormant. Per-seller long-term trust score: 12-36 months. Most per-listing state must be evictable on listing closure because listing_id cardinality is unbounded.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 30-100 features per inline write-path decision (seller-velocity + seller-rate-metrics + listing-image-history + brand-authorization + (seller, buyer) history + payout-account inverted-view + IP / device / location reputation + KYB-recency). Closer to the payments-fraud profile (20-100+) than the lighter T&S item 9 (10-40), because marketplace decisions span both T&S behavioural and financial-fraud dimensions. Strongly favours the batch_get path beava ships.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Crash-safe for the live counters that drive payout-hold / suspension decisions (a node losing its rolling 30d refund-rate window is hours of degraded enforcement and potential payout-loss). Regulator-grade for DSA / KYBC transparency reporting - but the regulator-grade artifact is the warehouse, not the in-memory counters. Beava's WAL + snapshot story comfortably covers the live-counter durability; the warehouse path is separate. Note that financial-ledger numbers (payout amounts, chargeback losses) must come from the ledger of record, not from beava.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Strong fit for single-binary regional / sidecar deployments next to the marketplace seller-action service or the moderation API. Per-region marketplaces (Vinted EU, Mercari JP/US, Depop, Whatnot US/EU, Reverb, Etsy) map cleanly onto a per-region beava deployment. Multi-region active-active is desired by the largest platforms (Amazon 3P, eBay, AliExpress, Walmart Marketplace, Facebook Marketplace) but not strictly required for a single-region deployment. Hard ceilings: beava v0 has no in-process sharding (single tenant beyond ~684k EPS or ~100-150 GB hot state must hand-shard externally), no native multi-tenancy (vendors like Sift, Forter, Riskified, Signifyd, ActiveFence/Alice serving many marketplaces on shared infrastructure have no isolation primitives), refuse-on-network-FS forces local-disk WAL planning, no built-in TLS/auth disqualifies internet-exposed deployments.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Marketplace Integrity / Seller Trust / Marketplace Risk / Trust & Safety engineering teams at (a) horizontal C2C / P2P resale marketplaces (eBay, Mercari, Vinted, Depop, Poshmark, OfferUp, Facebook Marketplace, Kijiji, Gumtree, Wallapop, Carousell, Vestiaire Collective, The RealReal, StockX, GOAT), (b) vertical and curated marketplaces (Etsy handmade/vintage, Reverb musical instruments, Discogs music collectibles, Whatnot livestream collectibles, 1stDibs antiques, Chrono24 watches, Sotheby's online, Heritage Auctions), (c) B2C 3P marketplaces (Amazon 3P, Walmart Marketplace, Target Plus, AliExpress, Allegro, Cdiscount, Bol.com, Coupang, MercadoLibre, Shopee, Lazada, Otto), (d) gig / services / food marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Instacart, Grubhub, TaskRabbit, Thumbtack, Fiverr, Upwork, Toptal), (e) travel and accommodation marketplaces with DSA exposure (Airbnb, Vrbo/Expedia, Booking.com, Vacasa), and (f) chargeback-guarantee / risk vendors who would embed beava as the feature backend (Riskified, Forter, Signifyd, Sift, NoFraud, Kount, Sardine, Unit21, Incognia, Persona, Trustpair on the B2B side, ActiveFence/Alice and Cinder on the T&S side). The buyer is Marketplace Integrity Eng / Seller Trust Platform / Marketplace Risk - distinct from the corporate Risk team, distinct from the buyer-side fraud team (item 1a), and distinct from the broader T&S UGC team (item 9).
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Marketplace fraud detection sits at the intersection of three sized markets: (1) Fraud Detection and Prevention overall - Mordor Intelligence pegs USD 55.98B in 2025 -> USD 70.19B in 2026 -> USD 171.84B by 2031; MarketsandMarkets USD 32.00B 2025 -> USD 65.68B 2030 at 15.5 % CAGR; Coherent Market Insights USD 52.06B 2026 -> USD 146.25B 2033 at 15.9 %. (2) Trust & Safety tooling - USD 10-15B in 2025 with 13-15 % CAGR through 2030. (3) E-commerce-fraud-prevention narrowly, projected to grow from low double-digit billions through 2030. Vendor scale signals: Sift processes ~1T events per year across the entire suite; Riskified is publicly traded (NYSE: RSKD) with hundreds of millions in annual revenue; Forter raised at USD 3B valuation; Signifyd raised at USD 1.4B valuation; ActiveFence/Alice protects 3B+ people and was valued >USD 500M in 2023; Incognia raised Series B in 2024-2025 with a stated marketplace-focus and 99.999999 % identification claim; Sardine raised USD 70M+ Series C in 2024. Regulatory spend drivers: Amazon publicly spent USD 1B+ on counterfeit/fraud protection in 2024 (Counterfeit Crimes Unit + Brand Registry + Project Zero); DSA non-compliance fines up to 6 % of global turnover; EU KYBC requirements on marketplaces under DSA Art. 30; UK OSA marketplace exposure; CNBC's 2025 investigation of Walmart Marketplace identity-theft and counterfeits drove a public board-level response. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) Regulation - EU DSA marketplace 'trader-traceability' obligations (KYBC / Art. 30) now in force; UK Online Safety Act exposure for marketplaces; the Commission's proposal in November 2025 to repeal P2B in favour of DSA/DMA enforcement; US INFORM Consumers Act in force (high-volume third-party seller verification); EU GPSR (General Product Safety Regulation) in force since December 2024 forcing marketplaces to take responsibility for unsafe products. 2) AI-driven seller fraud - Sumsub's 2025-2026 reports cite a 180 % YoY increase in multi-step coordinated attacks; LLM-generated listing copy and AI-generated counterfeit product images break heuristic detectors; the CNBC September 2025 Walmart Marketplace expose forced visible board-level attention. 3) Returns abuse - NRF estimates 7-10 % of returns are fraudulent costing US retailers USD 18B+ annually; Amazon's June 2024 returns-processing-fee policy and Q1 2026 tightening of returns / reviews / refunds; Walmart's parallel raising of Seller Performance Standards in 2026. 4) Chargeback losses - card-not-present chargebacks growing double-digits, pulling chargeback-guarantee vendors (Riskified, Forter, Signifyd) into the marketplace conversation. 5) Counterfeit / brand-protection pressure - eBay's 2023 acquisition of 3PM Shield, Amazon's USD 1B+ Counterfeit Crimes Unit spend in 2024, Walmart's 2024-2025 public AI investments in seller-detection. 6) Existing tooling pain - in-house teams running Redis + Lua + Flink for seller-velocity features publicly complain about ops overhead and cold-start risk.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: EU DSA (Reg. 2022/2065) marketplace-specific obligations: Art. 30 KYBC (trader traceability), Art. 31 conformity for marketplace product info, transparency reporting under Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 (quantitative templates, first harmonised reports early 2026). EU GPSR (Reg. 2023/988) - marketplaces must designate a 'responsible person' for products sold and act on RAPEX safety alerts (in force since 13 December 2024). US INFORM Consumers Act (in force June 2023) - high-volume third-party seller verification (>USD 5k gross revenue or >200 transactions in 12 months) including bank account, tax ID, government ID. EU AML 6th Directive / 6AMLD - relevant for payout-side onboarding. PSD2/PSD3 SCA on the buyer side, which collapses into item 1a. UK Online Safety Act marketplace exposure for illegal-content takedown. GDPR / CCPA on seller_id, IP, fingerprint, payout_account - argues for short TTL, hashing at rest, right-to-erasure. PCI-DSS on the payout/payment surface. SOC 2 Type II is table stakes for any marketplace-buyer's procurement. State-level US laws: California SB-301 (online marketplace high-volume seller info), various state INFORM-Consumers-style laws.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast - 2-5 days to a working per-seller listing-velocity + 30-day rolling refund-rate + per-(seller, buyer) collusion-pair demo on beava, since the @bv.event + @bv.table primitives map directly to the Amazon/Walmart/eBay public performance-metric definitions. A realistic 40-80-feature production pilot at a mid-sized marketplace is a 3-8 week effort once TLS, auth, and KYBC-aligned PII handling are added (the v0 gaps below). The 'seller-burst + refund-rate + image-reuse + ban-evasion' quadruple-demo is the obvious one-page README example for this vertical and complements the existing python/beava/demos/ecommerce demo on the buyer-side.

competition.incumbents: Generic real-time stack dominated by Redis (counters + Lua, Redis Stack with Bloom / CMS / Top-K modules) for velocity + rate features. Aerospike at very high cardinality (some retail / marketplace deployments). Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers with a Kafka backbone wanting SQL semantics - Riskified publicly uses Confluent ksqlDB + Flink DataStream API; many in-house teams (Etsy, eBay, Mercari, Walmart) run Kafka + Flink or Kafka + Spark Streaming + Redis for the live-feature layer. Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel / Feast as managed online feature stores feeding XGBoost / LightGBM seller-risk models. Postgres + materialized views at the small end (smaller niche marketplaces). DynamoDB / ScyllaDB for global multi-region marketplaces (Airbnb, Uber-style architectures). Specialised graph DBs (Neo4j, TigerGraph) for collusion / ring detection.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: End-to-end marketplace fraud / chargeback vendors (the buyer would procure these as black boxes that internally subsume the feature-store layer): Sift (Account Defense, Payment Protection, Content Integrity, Dispute Management - 16k+ signals, 1T events/year, G2 #1 in fraud detection Fall 2025), Forter (175M-identity database, automated yes/no decisions, Forter Element for PSPs), Riskified (Chargeback Guarantee, 480+ attributes per transaction, ksqlDB + Flink stack), Signifyd (Commerce Network, Intelligent Returns Protection, Seller Protect, Chargeback Guarantee), Kount (Equifax-owned, Identity Trust Global Network), NoFraud (real-time screening + analyst review), Sardine (marketplace fraud playbook, USD 70M+ Series C 2024). Marketplace-trust-specialists: Incognia (location-behavioral biometrics, Incognia ID, marketplace-seller-fraud playbook), Persona (KYB + onboarding for marketplaces, marketplace-regulation guide 2025), Trustpair (B2B payment-account verification), Sumsub (KYB / KYC / fraud, AI-Agent Verification 2026). T&S-as-a-service vendors that touch marketplace integrity: ActiveFence/Alice (3B+ users protected, marketplace solution page), Cinder (ex-Meta team), TrustLab (DSA/OSA compliance focused), Resolver (security + risk + compliance). Brand-protection / counterfeit-specific: 3PM Shield (acquired by eBay 2023), Doppel (fake-product-seller-detection), MarqVision (brand IP protection), Red Points, Corsearch. In-house equivalents at Amazon (Counterfeit Crimes Unit + Brand Registry + Project Zero + Amazon Fraud Detector), Walmart Marketplace (AI seller-detection, 2024-2025 public investments), eBay (Marketplace Integrity Team + 3PM Shield), Etsy (Trust & Safety ML eng team, reCAPTCHA Enterprise integration, Handmade & Counterfeit team), Mercari (predictive analytics, badge system, AI security team May 2025), Vinted Engineering, Airbnb Trust (Project Lighthouse for fairness, integrity ML). Beava more naturally sits underneath one of these vendors or an in-house equivalent than replaces them end-to-end.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster - fits the per-region / per-marketplace-vertical sidecar topology that vertical marketplaces (Reverb, Discogs, Whatnot, Vestiaire) actually deploy. 2) 50+ aggregation primitives natively cover the velocity / refund-rate / n_unique / distribution features marketplace integrity lives on, without writing Lua scripts or Flink SQL - directly addresses the Redis+Lua maintenance burden cited by mid-sized marketplaces. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get matches the inline seller-action submit budget that today is often bolted on asynchronously; closes the gap that lets drop-shipping / counterfeit-burst attacks complete before checks fire. 4) Native composite-key (pair / triple) aggregations - (seller, buyer), (seller, payout_account), (image_hash, n_unique seller_id), (ip_hash, n_unique seller_id) - which Redis requires hand-rolled hash-of-hash schemes for and which are *the* marketplace-integrity signals. 5) Apache-2.0, no open-core - attractive to chargeback-guarantee vendors (Riskified, Forter, Signifyd, Sift) and marketplace-fraud specialists (Incognia, Sardine, Sumsub) who want to embed it rather than depend on a competitor's managed cloud, and attractive to large in-house teams (eBay, Amazon, Walmart, Mercari, Etsy) who do not want vendor lock-in on integrity-critical control planes. 6) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON, framed TCP, msgpack) maps directly to how marketplace seller-action pipelines already shape events; no broker hop. 7) Distance primitive cleanly expresses impossible-travel between seller_signup and listing_create, and price-vs-category-median signals. 8) Sliding-window primitives over 30d / 60d / 90d windows align *exactly* with Amazon's, Walmart's, eBay's published performance-standard windows - the rare alignment between a generic feature store and a platform-specific enforcement metric.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS, no auth in v0 on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 - disqualifying for any production marketplace deployment; SOC 2 / DSA / INFORM-Consumers audit programs all require authenticated access to integrity infrastructure. 2) No in-process sharding - Amazon-3P-, eBay-, AliExpress-, Walmart-Marketplace-scale platforms exceed a single box; the single-tenant ceiling is roughly ~684k EPS and ~100-150 GB hot state. 3) Refuse-on-network-FS plus in-memory-only means buyers must plan local-disk WAL and bound cold-start replay time. 4) No triggers / 'fire when (seller_id).30d_refund_rate crosses 8 %' - marketplace integrity is inherently event-driven (auto-hold-payout, force returnless-refund, escalate-to-KYB-re-verification, suspend-seller), and today that has to be polled. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives - chargeback-guarantee vendors and T&S vendors serving many marketplaces on shared infrastructure need per-tenant namespaces, quotas, and per-tenant rate-limit accounting. 6) No secondary indexes / no 'list all sellers with 30d_refund_rate > 8 %' query - kills the analyst surface; Amazon Brand Registry, eBay Marketplace Integrity, Walmart Marketplace dashboards all expose this view today. 7) No native graph / pair-clustering primitives for collusion ring detection beyond first-order pair counters (Meta CIB, eBay 3PM Shield rely on multi-hop graph queries; beava can only push the per-(seller, buyer) pair and per-(seller, payout_account) pair grain). 8) No image-hash / pHash primitive built-in - buyer must compute the pHash / PDQ / NeuralHash externally and push the digest in; documenting the pattern is critical. 9) No native PII / right-to-erasure cascade story across all derived aggregates (GDPR Art. 17 is load-bearing on seller_id, beneficial_owner_hash). 10) No KYBC / INFORM-Consumers-style audit-log primitive (regulator-grade durability tier is a warehouse, not beava). 11) No native financial-ledger integration - payout-clawback decisions must reconcile against the ledger of record, not just against beava counters.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: seller-onboarding service (HTTP push), listing-create / edit service (HTTP push from the marketplace web/mobile gateway), order / payment / refund / chargeback service (HTTP or framed TCP from the checkout backend), message / comment / review service (HTTP from the messaging backend), KYB / identity-verification webhook (HTTP from Sumsub / Persona / Trulioo / Onfido), payment-processor webhook (Stripe Connect, Adyen for Platforms, PayPal Marketplaces, Mangopay), brand-protection feed (eBay 3PM Shield, Doppel, MarqVision, Amazon Brand Registry), perceptual-hash service (in-house PDQ / pHash workers feeding image_hash digests). Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits all webhook-style producers; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits the high-throughput listing-create gateway. Consumers: rules engines (in-house DSL / Drools / FEEL / Kestra workflow / Cinder workflow engine - 'if seller.30d_refund_rate > 8 % then hold payout'), ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM seller-risk, transformer-based listing-text classifiers, image-classification models for counterfeit detection), and inline allow / queue / friction logic in the seller-action RPC. Vendors that would consume beava: Sift, Forter, Riskified, Signifyd, Sardine, NoFraud, Incognia, Persona, Sumsub on the embed path; ActiveFence/Alice, Cinder on the T&S-platform embed path.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Marketplaces run deterministic rules (Amazon / Walmart / eBay performance-standard thresholds are explicit rules: 'if 30d_refund_rate > 8 % in category X then suspend') alongside ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM seller-risk, graph-based collusion-ring detection, image-similarity / pHash for counterfeit, transformer-based listing-text classifiers, ensembles like Riskified's 480+ attributes and Sift's 16k+ signals). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from the scorer - both the rules engine and the ML model read from the same batch_get path.

adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum. Marketplace supply-side abuse is one of the most actively adversarial domains in tech - counterfeiters, drop-shippers, fee-arbitrage rings, ban-evaders, refund-abuse rings, review-collusion clusters, and identity-theft sellers retool weekly. LLM-generated listing copy, AI-generated counterfeit product imagery, and synthetic-identity KYBC bypass are 2024-2026 escalations called out by Sumsub, Sift, and the CNBC Walmart investigation. Feature drift is fast; buyers expect to add and retire features continuously, which strongly argues for a developer-ergonomic feature backend (beava's @bv.event / @bv.table model) over a SQL-on-Flink pipeline that requires schema migrations. Roblox-style real-time multimodal review and Amazon's USD 1B+ annual counterfeit-protection spend show the order of magnitude of buyer investment when the integrity stack is taken seriously.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Image / NLP classification on raw listing content - that belongs in CV / transformer models (Hive, Doppel, MarqVision, in-house pHash + CNN ensembles), not beava. Beava counts the pHash but does not compute it. 2) KYB document verification itself - Sumsub / Persona / Onfido / Trulioo own that; beava can count KYB-re-verification velocity per seller. 3) Long historical lookback for DSA / INFORM-Consumers audits - beava is in-memory; that belongs in Parquet / a lakehouse. 4) Multi-hop graph clustering for collusion-ring detection ('cluster of sellers sharing payout-account / device / IP across 3+ hops') - beava has no join engine; that's a graph-DB / OLAP problem, although beava can serve per-cluster aggregates once a cluster_id is computed externally and pushed in. 5) Financial-ledger reconciliation for payout-clawback - beava's counters are not the source of truth for money. 6) Acting as the rules engine, the ML scorer, the case-management UI, or the chargeback-guarantee insurance underwriter - beava is the feature backend. 7) Strict regulator-grade durability for DSA / INFORM-Consumers reports - those numbers should be sourced from an auditable warehouse, not from in-memory counters. 8) Multi-region active-active in v0. 9) Buyer-side payment fraud detection - that is item 1a (CNP fraud); the seam between item 1a (buyer-side) and item 10 (seller-side) is intentional. 10) Cross-marketplace seller-identity reconciliation (a fraud-network spanning eBay+Etsy+Mercari simultaneously) - that requires an external consortium identity service like Sift's Global Network, Forter's 175M-identity DB, Signifyd's Commerce Network or Incognia's cross-app device intelligence; beava can store but not compute the cross-platform identity graph.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for marketplace integrity, roughly in priority order: 1) TLS termination and mutual TLS on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 plus an auth model (token, mTLS, or both) on the push and admin surfaces - without this, no DSA / INFORM-Consumers / SOC 2 compliant marketplace and no chargeback-guarantee vendor can deploy externally. Same blocker as items 1a / 9 and the single most important gap. 2) Triggers / 'fire callback when (seller_id).30d_refund_rate crosses category-threshold' - marketplace integrity is fundamentally event-driven (auto-hold-payout, force-returnless-refund, escalate-KYB, suspend-seller, claw-back), and polling 30-100 features per event just to threshold them wastes round-trips on the asynchronous path. 3) First-class composite-key (pair / triple) aggregations - (seller, buyer), (seller, payout_account), (image_hash, n_unique seller_id) inverted index, (ip_hash, n_unique seller_id), (brand_gtin, n_unique seller_id) - need to be ergonomic in the @bv.table DSL because these are the load-bearing marketplace-integrity signals. 4) HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K as first-class aggregations to keep listing_id / (seller, buyer) pair / image_hash cardinality in bounded RAM during counterfeit bursts; if these are already in the 50+ primitives, document them prominently with worked examples ('top-K image-hashes seen on the most distinct sellers in last 30 days'). 5) In-process or sidecar sharding by key prefix (seller_id, listing_id, image_hash) for Amazon-3P / eBay / AliExpress / Walmart scale. 6) Per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction aligned with platform performance windows (30d / 60d / 90d) so listing_id and (seller, buyer) cardinality stay bounded. 7) Multi-tenancy: per-tenant namespaces, quotas, per-tenant rate-limit accounting for vendors serving many marketplaces (Sift, Forter, Riskified, Signifyd, Incognia, Persona). 8) Streaming admin / debug surface + secondary indexes so marketplace integrity analysts can run 'top-K sellers by 30d_refund_rate' or 'top-K image_hashes seen on the most distinct sellers in last 30d' without materializing the whole keyspace - Amazon Brand Registry, eBay 3PM Shield, Walmart Marketplace dashboards all expose this view today. 9) PII-handling story: seller_id / IP / fingerprint / payout_account / beneficial_owner_hash hashing at rest, configurable per-namespace retention, right-to-erasure that cascades through all derived aggregates (GDPR Art. 17, DSA Art. 14, INFORM-Consumers). 10) Documented hooks for graph-cluster enrichment (external collusion-clustering job pushes cluster_id sidecar dimension into beava). 11) Image-hash integration pattern documented (sidecar to PDQ / pHash / NeuralHash workers, with beava counting per-pHash-prefix seller diversity). 12) Cold-start strategy: WAL replay on tens of GB of hot seller / listing state must be benchmarked and bounded. 13) Reference architecture for the seam between buyer-side CNP fraud (item 1a) and supply-side integrity (item 10) so the same beava deployment can serve both, with proper namespace isolation. 14) DSA / INFORM-Consumers / EU GPSR reference architecture (warehouse for transparency reports + beava for live counters) as a published opinionated pattern. 15) Native financial-ledger reconciliation hook documented (beava emits 'suspect refund-rate exceeded' triggers; ledger of record decides clawback).
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes - strongly. Marketplace integrity genuinely needs an event-driven trigger primitive ('when seller.30d_refund_rate crosses category-threshold (5-8 %) then hold payout and escalate'; 'when seller.listing_create_velocity_1h crosses N then throttle and queue for KYB re-verification'; 'when (image_hash).n_unique_seller_id_30d crosses 5 then flag all listings using this image_hash'; 'when (payout_account).n_unique_seller_id_30d crosses 3 then auto-hold payout pending review'). Polling 30-100 features per event to threshold them is workable on the inline write path because the read is already happening, but is wasteful and high-latency on the asynchronous payout-hold / suspension-review / claw-back path. This is one of the two most-cited gaps for the domain along with TLS + auth.
